QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_2

question.text: If USDINR spot is Rs 83, Indian risk-free rate is 7% and US risk-free rate is 5%, what is the theoretical 1-year USDINR futures price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Applying the Interest Rate Parity (IRP) formula F = S x (1 + RINR) / (1 + RUSD) to a 1-year horizon: 83 x 1.07 / 1.05 = 83 x 1.01905 = Rs 84.58. The futures price exceeds spot because the INR interest rate exceeds the USD rate, so USD trades at a forward premium. The Trap: Inverting the ratio produces Rs 81.42; adding the full 4% differential without proper compounding gives Rs 86.32; assuming futures equals spot ignores the interest-rate differential. Note: The workbook example on page 63 uses the same spot and rates for a 6-month tenor; the same IRP formula is applied here adapted to a 1-year period.
